Metadata.title: Dominik Huber – Full-Stack Developer
Metadata.description: Self-taught software developer from Germany, building fast, precise interfaces with Next.js, React and TypeScript.

HomePage.bio:
Hi 👋 I'm Dominik, a former automotive and engine engineering student at the <uni>University of Stuttgart</uni>. During the pandemic I taught myself programming, and I've been building software ever since, with a focus on interfaces that feel fast, precise and calm.

It started with <extensions>browser extensions</extensions> in plain <js>JavaScript</js>, and honestly a lot of wrestling with HTML and CSS, with great support from my team along the way. From there I moved into data: scraping pipelines in <python>Python</python> and <node>Node.js</node>. Eventually I found where I'm happiest: the frontend. Today I build with <next>Next.js</next>, <react>React</react> and <ts>TypeScript</ts>, and I care about the details you only notice when they're missing: type-safe APIs, accessible components, motion that supports instead of distracts, and interfaces that stay responsive under real data.

That foundation led me to build <profitpath>ProfitPath</profitpath>, an Amazon arbitrage platform that makes online arbitrage accessible for sellers. It processes data from 1,000+ companies and suppliers and 200M+ products updated daily, and turns it into tools like supplier search, wholesale scanning, competitor analysis and automated profit calculations. The hard part isn't the data, it's the UX: making millions of rows scannable, filterable and actionable in seconds. Want to know more? Reach out on <linkedin>LinkedIn</linkedin>

AboutPage.origin: I was born in Ulm, Germany, and I'm a passionate full-stack developer.

story.p1: I probably spend more time in front of a screen than I'd like to admit – but at least it's usually for a good reason. I love writing code, turning new ideas into something real and building, step by step, a thought into something that actually works in the end. Most of the time, anyway.
story.p2: My interest in technology goes far beyond programming, though. <apple>Apple</apple> in particular has won me over. I love good design, well-thought-out products and those small details that probably only delight people who spend far too long staring at user interfaces. So I usually follow new Apple products with a mix of excitement and the question of whether I really need them. We both probably know the answer.
story.p3: When I need a break from the screen, you'll often find me on the <golf>golf course</golf>. I like the mix of calm, focus and the fact that this sport regularly reminds you not to take yourself too seriously. Some days everything goes exactly as planned – and on others you're just happy to find your ball again.
story.p4: A completely different side of me is my passion for <latam>Latin America</latam>. I love the music, the culture, the joy of life and especially the energy that comes with it. Latin music is on pretty much all the time – whether I'm working, on the go, or when “just one song” has suddenly turned into an entire playlist.
story.p5: In the end, I'm probably a somewhat unusual mix: developer, Apple enthusiast, golfer and big fan of Latin American culture.
story.p6: And that mix actually describes me pretty well.
